explanation: Original source arrays for added taxa, preserved with first/last time ranges and native fields. Earlier 50 profiles were created with tax() calls and are faithfully represented in taxa.json.

version_3_profiles.name: Foraminifera
version_3_profiles.etym: Latin forāmen “opening” + ferre “to bear,” for pores in their tests.
version_3_profiles.what: Diverse amoeboid protists whose shells are abundant marine microfossils and proxies for ocean conditions.
version_3_profiles.traits: Granular reticulating pseudopodia; often chambered calcite tests; planktonic and benthic lifestyles.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Rhizaria
├─ Radiolaria
└─ Foraminifera
   ├─ Globigerinida (planktonic)
   └─ Miliolida (benthic)

version_3_profiles.name: Radiolaria
version_3_profiles.etym: Latin radiolus “little ray,” for their radial skeletal spines.
version_3_profiles.what: Mostly oceanic protists that produce complex silica skeletons preserved from the Paleozoic onward.
version_3_profiles.traits: Radiating axopodia, mineralized siliceous skeletons in many, marine planktonic feeding.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Rhizaria
├─ Foraminifera
└─ Radiolaria (sensu lato)
   ├─ Polycystinea
   └─ Acantharea

version_3_profiles.name: Diatoms (Bacillariophyta)
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek diá “through” + témnein “to cut,” referring to their two-part cell coverings.
version_3_profiles.what: Photosynthetic stramenopile algae with an extensive marine and freshwater fossil record, especially in the Cenozoic.
version_3_profiles.traits: Interlocking silica frustule halves; chloroplasts; major role in aquatic carbon fixation.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Stramenopiles
├─ Brown algae
└─ Diatoms (Bacillariophyta)
   ├─ Centric diatoms
   └─ Pennate diatoms

version_3_profiles.name: Dinoflagellata
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek dînos “whirling” + Latin flagellum “whip.”
version_3_profiles.what: Mostly planktonic alveolates, including photosynthetic, predatory and symbiotic species; cysts are important microfossils.
version_3_profiles.traits: Two differently oriented flagella in typical motile cells; some form cellulose plates or resistant cysts.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Alveolata
├─ Ciliates
└─ Dinoflagellata
   ├─ Dinophyceae
   └─ Other dinoflagellate lineages

version_3_profiles.name: Coccolithophores
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek kókkos “berry” + líthos “stone” + -phore “bearer.”
version_3_profiles.what: Oceanic haptophyte algae with calcite platelets; their remains contribute to chalk and deep-sea carbonate sediments.
version_3_profiles.traits: Microscopic overlapping coccolith plates; bloom-forming photosynthesis; key marine carbon cycle role.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Haptophyta
├─ Other haptophytes
└─ Coccolithophores
   ├─ Coccolithaceae
   └─ Noelaerhabdaceae

version_3_profiles.name: Stromatoporoidea
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek strôma “layer, covering” + póros “pore” + -oeidḗs “resembling.”
version_3_profiles.what: Extinct hypercalcified reef organisms generally interpreted as sponges; especially important in Silurian–Devonian reefs.
version_3_profiles.traits: Layered and pillar-like calcareous skeletons; reef-building colonial-looking growth forms.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Porifera
├─ Other sponge lineages
└─ Stromatoporoidea
   ├─ Ordovician stromatoporoids †
   └─ Devonian stromatoporoids †

version_3_profiles.name: Rhodophyta (red algae)
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek rhódon “rose” + phytón “plant.”
version_3_profiles.what: Primarily aquatic archaeplastid algae, with a fossil record extending well into the Proterozoic.
version_3_profiles.traits: Phycobilin pigments, typically no flagellated stages, and often complex multicellular life cycles.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Archaeplastida
├─ Green plants
└─ Rhodophyta (red algae)
   ├─ Bangiophyceae
   └─ Florideophyceae

version_3_profiles.name: Chlorophyta
version_3_profiles.tagline: Diverse freshwater and marine green algae
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek khlōrós “green” + phytón “plant.”
version_3_profiles.what: One of the two main branches of green plants, encompassing many freshwater, marine and unicellular forms.
version_3_profiles.traits: Chlorophyll a and b; starch in plastids; diverse unicellular, colonial and multicellular bodies.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Viridiplantae
├─ Streptophyta (land-plant lineage)
└─ Chlorophyta
   ├─ Chlorophyceae
   └─ Ulvophyceae

version_3_profiles.name: Embryophyta (land plants)
version_3_profiles.tagline: Plants adapted to life on land
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek émbryon “young organism” + phytón “plant,” referring to retained embryos.
version_3_profiles.what: The terrestrial branch of green plants; liverworts, mosses, vascular plants and their fossil relatives.
version_3_profiles.traits: Multicellular protected embryos; cuticle and sporopollenin adaptations in many lineages.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Streptophyta
├─ Charophyte green algae
└─ Embryophyta (land plants)
   ├─ Bryophyte lineages
   └─ Tracheophyta (vascular plants)

version_3_profiles.name: Bryophytes (nonvascular land plants)
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek brýon “moss” + phytón “plant.”
version_3_profiles.what: Early-diverging land-plant lineages, important in moist habitats and soil formation.
version_3_profiles.traits: No lignified vascular system like tracheophytes; sporophyte dependent on gametophyte in most.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Embryophyta
├─ Tracheophyta
└─ Bryophytes (nonvascular land plants)
   ├─ Mosses
   └─ Liverworts and hornworts

version_3_profiles.name: Lycophyta
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek lýkos “wolf” + phytón “plant,” via clubmoss names.
version_3_profiles.what: Ancient vascular-plant branch that included tree-sized coal-swamp plants and survives as clubmosses and relatives.
version_3_profiles.traits: Microphyll leaves with single veins; spore-bearing structures; some fossil arborescent forms.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Tracheophyta
├─ Euphyllophytes
└─ Lycophyta
   ├─ Lycopodiales
   └─ Isoetales and Selaginellales

version_3_profiles.name: Equisetales (horsetails)
version_3_profiles.etym: Latin equus “horse” + saeta “bristle,” reflected in Equisetum.
version_3_profiles.what: Spore-bearing vascular plants with extinct tree-sized relatives prominent in Carboniferous wetlands.
version_3_profiles.traits: Hollow jointed stems, whorled branch pattern, silica deposits and terminal spore cones.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Monilophytes
├─ True ferns
└─ Equisetales (horsetails)
   ├─ Calamitaceae †
   └─ Equisetaceae

version_3_profiles.name: Glossopteridales
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek glôssa “tongue” + pterís “fern,” for tongue-shaped leaves.
version_3_profiles.what: Extinct seed-plant assemblage important in Permian Gondwanan coal floras and continental-drift evidence.
version_3_profiles.traits: Glossopteris-type net-veined leaves; seed-bearing organs; distribution on southern continents.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Seed plants
├─ Living gymnosperm branches
└─ Glossopteridales
   ├─ Glossopteris †
   └─ Gangamopteris †

version_3_profiles.name: Cycadales
version_3_profiles.tagline: Cone-bearing seed plants with stout trunks
version_3_profiles.etym: From Cycas, ultimately Greek kýkas, a name historically applied to palms.
version_3_profiles.what: An ancient gymnosperm lineage with major Mesozoic diversification; extant cycads survive mainly in warmer regions.
version_3_profiles.traits: Stout stems, pinnate leaves, separate male/female reproductive structures on most species.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Gymnosperms
├─ Conifer and ginkgo lineages
└─ Cycadales
   ├─ Cycadaceae
   └─ Zamiaceae

version_3_profiles.name: Ginkgoales
version_3_profiles.etym: Order named for Ginkgo, from a Japanese rendering of Chinese “silver apricot.”
version_3_profiles.what: Seed-plant order diverse in the Mesozoic, now represented by a single living species, Ginkgo biloba.
version_3_profiles.traits: Fan-shaped leaves with dichotomous veins; motile sperm retained in living ginkgo.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Gymnosperms
├─ Cycad and conifer lineages
└─ Ginkgoales
   ├─ Extinct ginkgo relatives †
   └─ Ginkgo biloba

version_3_profiles.name: Bennettitales
version_3_profiles.etym: Named for botanist John Joseph Bennett; botanical order suffix -ales.
version_3_profiles.what: Extinct seed plants resembling cycads in foliage, often with elaborate reproductive organs.
version_3_profiles.traits: Pinnate foliage in many; complex flower-like reproductive structures, not true angiosperm flowers.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Seed plants
├─ Living gymnosperm clades
└─ Bennettitales
   ├─ Bennettites †
   └─ Williamsonia †

version_3_profiles.name: Monocotyledons
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek mónos “one” + kotylēdṓn “seed leaf.”
version_3_profiles.what: A major flowering-plant lineage, prominent in Cretaceous and Cenozoic terrestrial ecosystems.
version_3_profiles.traits: A single embryonic cotyledon, often parallel leaf veins and floral parts in threes.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Angiosperms
├─ Eudicots and magnoliids
└─ Monocotyledons
   ├─ Early-diverging monocots
   └─ Commelinids (including grasses)

version_3_profiles.name: Eudicots
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek eû “true” + di- “two” + cotyledon; eudicot distinguishes a modern phylogenetic clade.
version_3_profiles.what: Large flowering-plant radiation including roses, sunflowers, oaks and beans.
version_3_profiles.traits: Tricolpate or derived pollen patterns; generally two embryonic seed leaves.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Angiosperms
├─ Monocots / magnoliids
└─ Eudicots
   ├─ Early-diverging eudicots
   └─ Core eudicots

version_3_profiles.name: Ctenophora
version_3_profiles.tagline: Comb jellies with ciliary swimming rows
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek kteís, ktenós “comb” + phérein “to carry.”
version_3_profiles.what: Gelatinous marine predators; their precise deepest animal-tree placement is actively debated.
version_3_profiles.traits: Eight comb rows made of fused cilia; sticky colloblast prey-capture cells in many.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Metazoa (deep branching uncertain)
├─ Sponges / cnidarians / bilaterians
└─ Ctenophora
   ├─ Tentaculata
   └─ Nuda

version_3_profiles.name: Priapulida
version_3_profiles.etym: Priapus, Greek fertility deity, plus diminutive -ul- and group suffix.
version_3_profiles.what: Marine ecdysozoans important in Cambrian soft-bodied faunas and sediment ecosystems.
version_3_profiles.traits: Reversible toothed proboscis (introvert), cuticle, molting and burrowing lifestyle.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Ecdysozoa
├─ Panarthropoda
└─ Priapulida
   ├─ Priapulopsis
   └─ Priapulus

version_3_profiles.name: Onychophora
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek ónyx “claw” + phérein “to bear.”
version_3_profiles.what: Soft-bodied terrestrial animals related to arthropods; Cambrian lobopodians illuminate their broader stem history.
version_3_profiles.traits: Paired unjointed legs with terminal claws; adhesive slime hunting; molting.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Panarthropoda
├─ Tardigrada and arthropod lineages
└─ Onychophora
   ├─ Peripatidae
   └─ Peripatopsidae

version_3_profiles.name: Myriapoda
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek myríos “countless” + poús “foot.”
version_3_profiles.what: Centipedes, millipedes and relatives, among the earliest animal lineages to establish terrestrial ecosystems.
version_3_profiles.traits: Numerous segments, one pair of antennae, uniramous walking legs in many.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Arthropoda
├─ Pancrustacea and Chelicerata
└─ Myriapoda
   ├─ Chilopoda (centipedes)
   └─ Diplopoda (millipedes)

version_3_profiles.name: Eurypterida
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek eurýs “broad” + pterón “wing,” for broad swimming appendages.
version_3_profiles.what: Extinct chelicerates, including some of the largest arthropods known, most abundant in Silurian–Devonian ecosystems.
version_3_profiles.traits: Chelicerae, armored segmented bodies, often paddle-like hind limbs and large chelate appendages.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Chelicerata
├─ Arachnids and horseshoe-crab lineages
└─ Eurypterida
   ├─ Eurypterina †
   └─ Stylonurina †

version_3_profiles.name: Decapoda
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek déka “ten” + poús “foot.”
version_3_profiles.what: Shrimps, crabs, lobsters and crayfish; a diverse crustacean group with extensive Mesozoic–Cenozoic radiations.
version_3_profiles.traits: Five pairs of thoracic walking limbs; carapace enclosing fused head/thorax in typical forms.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Pancrustacea
├─ Other crustacean branches
└─ Decapoda
   ├─ Dendrobranchiata (many shrimps)
   └─ Pleocyemata (crabs, lobsters)

version_3_profiles.name: Belemnitida
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek bélemnon “dart, missile,” for bullet-shaped fossil guards.
version_3_profiles.what: Extinct marine coleoids whose hard internal rostra are abundant Jurassic and Cretaceous fossils.
version_3_profiles.traits: Internal calcitic guard, muscular mantle, grasping arms and ink sacs in many known fossils.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Cephalopoda
├─ Ammonoids and nautiloids
└─ Belemnitida
   ├─ Belemnitina †
   └─ Belemnopseina †

version_3_profiles.name: Nautiloidea
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek nautílos “sailor,” historically applied to the chambered nautilus.
version_3_profiles.what: A long-ranging assemblage of shelled cephalopods, with Nautilus and Allonautilus as living representatives.
version_3_profiles.traits: Chambered buoyancy shell, siphuncle and many oral tentacles in extant nautilids.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Cephalopoda
├─ Coleoids and ammonoids
└─ Nautiloidea
   ├─ Extinct straight-shelled nautiloids †
   └─ Nautilida

version_3_profiles.name: Gastropoda
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek gastḗr “belly” + poús “foot.”
version_3_profiles.what: One of the largest molluscan radiations, with abundant marine, freshwater and terrestrial fossil records.
version_3_profiles.traits: Muscular crawling foot; torsion during development in most; often single coiled shell.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Mollusca
├─ Bivalves and cephalopods
└─ Gastropoda
   ├─ Patellogastropoda (limpets)
   └─ Caenogastropoda and Heterobranchia

version_3_profiles.name: Bivalvia
version_3_profiles.etym: Latin bi- “two” + valva “leaf of a folding door.”
version_3_profiles.what: Two-shelled molluscs important in Paleozoic to modern marine and freshwater habitats.
version_3_profiles.traits: Two hinged valves, mantle and gills; mostly suspension feeding and no adult radula.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Mollusca
├─ Gastropods and cephalopods
└─ Bivalvia
   ├─ Protobranchia
   └─ Autobranchia

version_3_profiles.name: Scleractinia
version_3_profiles.tagline: Stony corals that build modern reefs
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek sklērós “hard” + aktís “ray,” for radiating hard skeletal partitions.
version_3_profiles.what: Stony coral order prominent in post-Permian reef systems; numerous forms host photosynthetic symbionts.
version_3_profiles.traits: Aragonitic external skeletons with septa; polyps can form large reef colonies.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Cnidaria
├─ Soft corals and anemones
└─ Scleractinia
   ├─ Robust corals
   └─ Complex corals

version_3_profiles.name: Crinoidea
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek krínon “lily” + -oeidḗs “resembling.”
version_3_profiles.what: Filter-feeding echinoderms particularly abundant as Paleozoic skeletal fossils; feather stars still flourish.
version_3_profiles.traits: Five or more feathery arms, calcareous ossicles, and stalk in many fossil sea lilies.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Echinodermata
├─ Sea stars / sea urchins
└─ Crinoidea
   ├─ Stalked sea lilies
   └─ Feather stars

version_3_profiles.name: Echinoidea
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek ekhînos “hedgehog, sea urchin” + -oeidḗs “resembling.”
version_3_profiles.what: Marine echinoderms that diversify greatly from the Mesozoic onward, with many useful fossil forms.
version_3_profiles.traits: Rigid test of fused plates, mobile spines and a five-part jaw apparatus in many regular urchins.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Echinodermata
├─ Sea stars / crinoids
└─ Echinoidea
   ├─ Regular sea urchins
   └─ Irregular urchins (sand dollars)

version_3_profiles.name: Osteostraci
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek ostéon “bone” + óstrakon “shell.”
version_3_profiles.what: Extinct armored jawless vertebrates close to the jawed-vertebrate stem, abundant in Silurian–Devonian waters.
version_3_profiles.traits: Broad bony head shields, paired sensory fields and fins in many later forms.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Vertebrata
├─ Cyclostomes (living lampreys and hagfish)
└─ Osteostraci
   ├─ Cephalaspidida †
   └─ Other osteostracans †

version_3_profiles.name: Dipnoi (lungfishes)
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek dís “twice” + pnoḗ “breathing,” referring to gill and lung respiration.
version_3_profiles.what: Sarcopterygians with lungs; living lungfishes are among the closest living fish relatives of tetrapods.
version_3_profiles.traits: True lungs, tooth plates in most forms and fleshy paired fins.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Sarcopterygii
├─ Coelacanth lineage
└─ Dipnoi (lungfishes)
   ├─ Fossil dipnoans †
   └─ Living lungfishes

version_3_profiles.name: Actinistia (coelacanths)
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek aktís “ray,” referring to skeletal fin supports.
version_3_profiles.what: Coelacanth lineage widespread in the fossil record and surviving today as Latimeria species.
version_3_profiles.traits: Three-lobed caudal fin, distinctive paired lobe fins, intracranial joint in living forms.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Sarcopterygii
├─ Lungfishes and tetrapods
└─ Actinistia (coelacanths)
   ├─ Fossil coelacanth lineages †
   └─ Latimeriidae

version_3_profiles.name: Temnospondyli
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek témnein “cut” + spóndylos “vertebra.”
version_3_profiles.what: Diverse Paleozoic–Mesozoic tetrapods; some hypotheses place modern amphibians within this lineage.
version_3_profiles.traits: Typically complex multipart vertebrae, broad flattened skulls and aquatic larvae in many forms.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Early tetrapods
├─ Amniote stem
└─ Temnospondyli
   ├─ Edopoidea †
   └─ Stereospondyli †

version_3_profiles.name: Dicynodontia
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek dís “two” + kynó- “dog” + odoús “tooth,” for paired tusks in many forms.
version_3_profiles.what: Mostly herbivorous non-mammalian therapsids that survived and radiated after the end-Permian extinction.
version_3_profiles.traits: Keratinous beak, enlarged tusks in many species, sturdy limbs and reduced tooth rows.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Therapsida
├─ Cynodont lineage
└─ Dicynodontia
   ├─ Permian dicynodonts †
   └─ Triassic dicynodonts †

version_3_profiles.name: Gorgonopsia
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek Gorgṓn “Gorgon” + ópsis “appearance.”
version_3_profiles.what: Predatory synapsids that occupied terrestrial ecosystems late in the Permian and vanished at the end-Permian extinction.
version_3_profiles.traits: Large saber-like upper canines, differentiated dentition and relatively long limbs.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Therapsida
├─ Dicynodont and cynodont lineages
└─ Gorgonopsia
   ├─ Gorgonopsidae †
   └─ Other gorgonopsians †

version_3_profiles.name: Cynodontia
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek kýōn, kynós “dog” + odoús “tooth.”
version_3_profiles.what: Synapsid lineage including extinct non-mammalian cynodonts and all living mammals.
version_3_profiles.traits: Progressively complex chewing teeth, secondary palate in many and mammalian jaw/ear transitions.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Therapsida
├─ Dicynodonts and gorgonopsians
└─ Cynodontia
   ├─ Non-mammalian cynodonts †
   └─ Mammalia

version_3_profiles.name: Archosauria
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek arkhós “ruler” + saûros “lizard.”
version_3_profiles.what: Diapsid reptiles including crocodilians, birds and their extinct relatives such as dinosaurs and pterosaurs.
version_3_profiles.traits: Antorbital fenestra ancestrally; distinctive ankle and limb developments within the group.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Sauropsida
├─ Lepidosaurs and turtles
└─ Archosauria
   ├─ Pseudosuchia (crocodile line)
   └─ Avemetatarsalia (bird line)

version_3_profiles.name: Theropoda
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek thēríon “beast” + poús “foot.”
version_3_profiles.what: Dinosaur lineage encompassing predatory giants, small feathered species and all living birds.
version_3_profiles.traits: Hollow bones common, three main weight-bearing toes ancestral and feathers in many lineages.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Dinosauria
├─ Sauropodomorpha
└─ Theropoda
   ├─ Non-avian theropods †
   └─ Avialae → birds

version_3_profiles.name: Sauropoda
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek saûros “lizard” + poús “foot.”
version_3_profiles.what: Massive quadrupedal dinosaurs that diversified in Jurassic and Cretaceous terrestrial ecosystems.
version_3_profiles.traits: Long neck, columnar limbs, tiny skull relative to body and air-sac-linked axial pneumaticity in many.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Dinosauria
├─ Theropoda
└─ Sauropoda
   ├─ Diplodocoidea †
   └─ Macronaria †

version_3_profiles.name: Ornithischia
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek órnis “bird” + iskḥíon “hip,” describing a bird-like pelvic arrangement.
version_3_profiles.what: Predominantly herbivorous non-avian dinosaurs including stegosaurs, ankylosaurs, ceratopsians and hadrosaurs.
version_3_profiles.traits: Backward-pointing pubis in the traditional diagnosis and predentary beak bone in many.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Dinosauria
├─ Saurischia
└─ Ornithischia
   ├─ Thyreophora †
   └─ Ornithopoda and Marginocephalia †

version_3_profiles.name: Ceratopsia
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek kéras “horn” + ópsis “face.”
version_3_profiles.what: Ornithischian dinosaurs that diversified especially in the Late Cretaceous of Asia and North America.
version_3_profiles.traits: Beaks and cheek teeth; enlarged frills and horns in many derived ceratopsids.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Ornithischia
├─ Ornithopoda and stegosaurs
└─ Ceratopsia
   ├─ Early ceratopsians †
   └─ Ceratopsidae †

version_3_profiles.name: Hadrosauridae
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek hadrós “stout, bulky” + saûros “lizard,” with family suffix -idae.
version_3_profiles.what: Derived ornithopods particularly widespread in Late Cretaceous floodplain ecosystems.
version_3_profiles.traits: Wide beaks, dental batteries with many replacement teeth and complex chewing motions.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Ornithopoda
├─ Iguanodontian relatives
└─ Hadrosauridae
   ├─ Saurolophinae †
   └─ Lambeosaurinae †

version_3_profiles.name: Ichthyosauria
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek ikhthýs “fish” + saûros “lizard.”
version_3_profiles.what: Extinct air-breathing marine diapsids, especially diverse in Triassic–Jurassic seas.
version_3_profiles.traits: Fish- or dolphin-like bodies, limbs modified as paddles and very large eyes in several forms.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Diapsida
├─ Sauropterygia and other diapsids
└─ Ichthyosauria
   ├─ Early ichthyosauriforms †
   └─ Ophthalmosauridae †

version_3_profiles.name: Plesiosauria
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek plēsíos “near” + saûros “lizard,” originally noting resemblance to reptiles.
version_3_profiles.what: Marine sauropterygians widespread in Jurassic and Cretaceous oceans, with many long- and short-necked forms.
version_3_profiles.traits: Two pairs of powerful flippers; stiff trunks; varied neck proportions and head sizes.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Sauropterygia
├─ Nothosaur relatives
└─ Plesiosauria
   ├─ Plesiosauroidea †
   └─ Pliosauroidea †

version_3_profiles.name: Mosasauridae
version_3_profiles.etym: Latin Mosa “Meuse River” + Greek saûros “lizard,” with -idae family ending.
version_3_profiles.what: Extinct aquatic lizards closely related to living squamate lineages; prominent Late Cretaceous marine predators.
version_3_profiles.traits: Streamlined bodies, paddle-shaped limbs, laterally compressed tail and flexible skull joints.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Squamata
├─ Other lizard and snake branches
└─ Mosasauridae
   ├─ Mosasaurinae †
   └─ Tylosaurinae †

version_3_profiles.name: Enantiornithes
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek enantíos “opposite” + órnis “bird,” for a distinctive shoulder articulation.
version_3_profiles.what: Extinct birds widespread in Cretaceous terrestrial ecosystems, outside the lineage of living crown birds.
version_3_profiles.traits: Feathers and flight structures; often toothed jaws, clawed wings and an unusual shoulder joint.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Avialae
├─ Ornithuromorpha (modern-bird line)
└─ Enantiornithes
   ├─ Early enantiornithines †
   └─ Derived enantiornithines †

version_3_profiles.name: Monotremata
version_3_profiles.etym: Greek mónos “single” + trêma “opening,” for a cloaca.
version_3_profiles.what: Living platypuses and echidnas, an early-diverging branch of crown mammals.
version_3_profiles.traits: Egg laying, milk production without nipples, electrosensory snout in platypus.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Mammalia
├─ Theria (marsupials, placentals)
└─ Monotremata
   ├─ Ornithorhynchidae
   └─ Tachyglossidae

version_3_profiles.name: Proboscidea
version_3_profiles.etym: Latin proboscis “trunk, elongated nose.”
version_3_profiles.what: Mammalian order encompassing elephants and extinct mammoths, mastodons and early African relatives.
version_3_profiles.traits: Muscular trunk, continuously replacing cheek teeth in many derived lineages and enlarged incisors forming tusks.
version_3_profiles.clade:
Afrotheria
├─ Sirenia and hyraxes
└─ Proboscidea
   ├─ Early proboscideans †
   └─ Elephantidae

version_4_profiles.name: Bacteria
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek baktērion, little rod
version_4_profiles.what: Prokaryotes lacking a membrane-bound nucleus. Peptidoglycan walls in many lineages; enormous biochemical diversity.
version_4_profiles.traits: Peptidoglycan walls in many lineages; enormous biochemical diversity.

version_4_profiles.name: Pseudomonadota
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek pseudēs, false, and monas, unit; formerly Proteobacteria
version_4_profiles.what: Highly varied Gram-negative bacteria. Outer membrane; many nitrogen and sulfur cyclers.
version_4_profiles.traits: Outer membrane; many nitrogen and sulfur cyclers.

version_4_profiles.name: Actinomycetota
version_4_profiles.tagline: Filamentous soil bacteria and antibiotic producers
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek aktis, ray, and mykēs, fungus
version_4_profiles.what: Filamentous soil bacteria and antibiotic producers. High-GC genomes; branching growth in many forms.
version_4_profiles.traits: High-GC genomes; branching growth in many forms.

version_4_profiles.name: Bacillota
version_4_profiles.etym: Latin bacillus, little staff
version_4_profiles.what: Endospore-forming and fermenting bacteria. Thick cell walls in many members; diverse metabolism.
version_4_profiles.traits: Thick cell walls in many members; diverse metabolism.

version_4_profiles.name: Methanobacteria
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek methy, wine, and archaeal bacterial naming
version_4_profiles.what: Methane-producing archaea. Methanogenesis in oxygen-poor habitats.
version_4_profiles.traits: Methanogenesis in oxygen-poor habitats.

version_4_profiles.name: Halobacteria
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek hals, salt, and bakterion, rod
version_4_profiles.what: Salt-loving archaea. Light-driven rhodopsins; high-salinity adaptations.
version_4_profiles.traits: Light-driven rhodopsins; high-salinity adaptations.

version_4_profiles.name: Haptophyta
version_4_profiles.tagline: Marine algae with tiny calcite plates
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek haptein, attach, and phyton, plant
version_4_profiles.what: Marine algae with tiny calcite plates. Often possess a haptonema; some produce coccoliths.
version_4_profiles.traits: Often possess a haptonema; some produce coccoliths.

version_4_profiles.name: Cryptophyta
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek kryptos, hidden, and phyton, plant
version_4_profiles.what: Flagellate algae with specialized plastids. Two unequal flagella; distinctive nucleomorph in some.
version_4_profiles.traits: Two unequal flagella; distinctive nucleomorph in some.

version_4_profiles.name: Charophyta
version_4_profiles.tagline: Green algae closest to land plants
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek chara, joy; name associated with stoneworts
version_4_profiles.what: Green algae closest to land plants. Cellulose walls and land-plant-like cell machinery.
version_4_profiles.traits: Cellulose walls and land-plant-like cell machinery.

version_4_profiles.name: Choanoflagellatea
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek choanē, funnel, and Latin flagellum, whip
version_4_profiles.what: Single-celled relatives of animals. Flagellum ringed by feeding microvilli.
version_4_profiles.traits: Flagellum ringed by feeding microvilli.

version_4_profiles.name: Ciliophora
version_4_profiles.etym: Latin cilium, eyelash, and Greek phoros, bearing
version_4_profiles.what: Protists propelled by cilia. Two functionally distinct nuclei and coordinated cilia.
version_4_profiles.traits: Two functionally distinct nuclei and coordinated cilia.

version_4_profiles.name: Apicomplexa
version_4_profiles.etym: Latin apex, tip, and complexus, intertwined
version_4_profiles.what: Obligately parasitic alveolates. Apical cell-invasion apparatus; complex life cycles.
version_4_profiles.traits: Apical cell-invasion apparatus; complex life cycles.

version_4_profiles.name: Tracheophyta
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek tracheia, windpipe, and phyton, plant
version_4_profiles.what: Plants with vascular conducting tissues. Xylem and phloem allow upright growth.
version_4_profiles.traits: Xylem and phloem allow upright growth.

version_4_profiles.name: Rhyniophyta
version_4_profiles.etym: Named for Rhynie, Scotland
version_4_profiles.what: Early simple-stemmed vascular plants. Forked naked axes with terminal sporangia.
version_4_profiles.traits: Forked naked axes with terminal sporangia.

version_4_profiles.name: Zosterophyllopsida
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek zostēr, belt, and phyllon, leaf
version_4_profiles.what: Extinct early lycophyte relatives. Lateral sporangia and branching stems.
version_4_profiles.traits: Lateral sporangia and branching stems.

version_4_profiles.name: Progymnospermopsida
version_4_profiles.tagline: Woody spore-bearing trees before seed plants
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek pro, before, and gymnos, naked seed
version_4_profiles.what: Woody spore-bearing trees before seed plants. Secondary wood and fernlike reproduction.
version_4_profiles.traits: Secondary wood and fernlike reproduction.

version_4_profiles.name: Archaeopteridales
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek archaios, ancient, and pteris, fern
version_4_profiles.what: Devonian trees with fernlike foliage. Trunk-forming forests; branches shedding leafy shoots.
version_4_profiles.traits: Trunk-forming forests; branches shedding leafy shoots.

version_4_profiles.name: Medullosales
version_4_profiles.etym: Latin medulla, pith
version_4_profiles.what: Seed ferns of Carboniferous forests. Large fronds with seeds rather than spores.
version_4_profiles.traits: Large fronds with seeds rather than spores.

version_4_profiles.name: Isoetales
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek isos, equal, and etos, year
version_4_profiles.what: Quillworts and extinct tree lycopsids. Ligules; subterranean corms in living quillworts.
version_4_profiles.traits: Ligules; subterranean corms in living quillworts.

version_4_profiles.name: Marattiales
version_4_profiles.etym: Named for Italian botanist Giovanni Maratti
version_4_profiles.what: Large tropical eusporangiate ferns. Massive fronds and thick-walled sporangia.
version_4_profiles.traits: Massive fronds and thick-walled sporangia.

version_4_profiles.name: Polypodiales
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek polys, many, and podion, little foot
version_4_profiles.what: Most familiar modern ferns. Leptosporangia and diverse sori patterns.
version_4_profiles.traits: Leptosporangia and diverse sori patterns.

version_4_profiles.name: Gnetales
version_4_profiles.etym: From the genus Gnetum
version_4_profiles.what: Unusual living gymnosperms. Vessel elements in many members; distinctive cones.
version_4_profiles.traits: Vessel elements in many members; distinctive cones.

version_4_profiles.name: Pinaceae
version_4_profiles.etym: Latin pinus, pine
version_4_profiles.what: Pines, spruces, firs and relatives. Woody cones and needlelike foliage.
version_4_profiles.traits: Woody cones and needlelike foliage.

version_4_profiles.name: Cupressaceae
version_4_profiles.etym: Latin cupressus, cypress
version_4_profiles.what: Cypresses, junipers and redwoods. Usually scale leaves; resinous wood.
version_4_profiles.traits: Usually scale leaves; resinous wood.

version_4_profiles.name: Araucariaceae
version_4_profiles.etym: Named after the Araucanía region of Chile
version_4_profiles.what: Ancient southern conifers. Massive trunks; broad or awl-like leaves.
version_4_profiles.traits: Massive trunks; broad or awl-like leaves.

version_4_profiles.name: Magnoliids
version_4_profiles.etym: Named from the magnolia lineage
version_4_profiles.what: Early-diverging flowering plant lineages. Fragrant oils; often spiral floral parts.
version_4_profiles.traits: Fragrant oils; often spiral floral parts.

version_4_profiles.name: Rosids
version_4_profiles.etym: From Rosa, rose, with -ids for a lineage
version_4_profiles.what: Major branch of eudicot flowers. Includes roses, legumes and oaks.
version_4_profiles.traits: Includes roses, legumes and oaks.

version_4_profiles.name: Asterids
version_4_profiles.etym: From Aster, star-like flower
version_4_profiles.what: Major branch of advanced eudicots. Often fused petals; many sympetalous flowers.
version_4_profiles.traits: Often fused petals; many sympetalous flowers.

version_4_profiles.name: Orchidaceae
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek orchis, testicle, for paired tubers
version_4_profiles.what: Orchids with highly specialized flowers. Pollinia and intricate pollinator relationships.
version_4_profiles.traits: Pollinia and intricate pollinator relationships.

version_4_profiles.name: Asteraceae
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek astēr, star
version_4_profiles.what: Daisies, sunflowers and composites. Heads of many tiny florets mimic a flower.
version_4_profiles.traits: Heads of many tiny florets mimic a flower.

version_4_profiles.name: Fabaceae
version_4_profiles.etym: Latin faba, bean
version_4_profiles.what: Legumes and nitrogen-fixing allies. Pods; root nodules in many lineages.
version_4_profiles.traits: Pods; root nodules in many lineages.

version_4_profiles.name: Arecaceae
version_4_profiles.tagline: Palms of tropical and warm regions
version_4_profiles.etym: Latin areca, palm name
version_4_profiles.what: Palms of tropical and warm regions. Unbranched trunks in many species; large leaves.
version_4_profiles.traits: Unbranched trunks in many species; large leaves.

version_4_profiles.name: Hexactinellida
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek hex, six, and aktis, ray
version_4_profiles.what: Glass sponges with silica frameworks. Six-rayed siliceous spicules; syncytial tissues.
version_4_profiles.traits: Six-rayed siliceous spicules; syncytial tissues.

version_4_profiles.name: Demospongiae
version_4_profiles.tagline: Most living marine and freshwater sponges
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek dēmos, people, and spongos, sponge
version_4_profiles.what: Most living marine and freshwater sponges. Spongin and/or silica skeletal elements.
version_4_profiles.traits: Spongin and/or silica skeletal elements.

version_4_profiles.name: Anthozoa
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek anthos, flower, and zōon, animal
version_4_profiles.what: Sea anemones and corals. Polyp-only cnidarian life cycle.
version_4_profiles.traits: Polyp-only cnidarian life cycle.

version_4_profiles.name: Hydrozoa
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek hydra, water serpent, and zōon, animal
version_4_profiles.what: Hydras, hydroids and siphonophores. Polyp and medusa phases in many lineages.
version_4_profiles.traits: Polyp and medusa phases in many lineages.

version_4_profiles.name: Scyphozoa
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek skyphos, cup, and zōon, animal
version_4_profiles.what: True jellyfish. Prominent swimming medusa with stinging cells.
version_4_profiles.traits: Prominent swimming medusa with stinging cells.

version_4_profiles.name: Placozoa
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek plakous, flat cake, and zōon, animal
version_4_profiles.what: Extremely simple flattened animals. Few cell types and ciliated creeping bodies.
version_4_profiles.traits: Few cell types and ciliated creeping bodies.

version_4_profiles.name: Nematoda
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek nēma, thread, and -odes, resembling
version_4_profiles.what: Roundworms in nearly all ecosystems. Nonsegmented tubular body and molting cuticle.
version_4_profiles.traits: Nonsegmented tubular body and molting cuticle.

version_4_profiles.name: Tardigrada
version_4_profiles.etym: Latin tardus, slow, and gradus, step
version_4_profiles.what: Microscopic eight-legged water bears. Cryptobiosis and stubby clawed appendages.
version_4_profiles.traits: Cryptobiosis and stubby clawed appendages.

version_4_profiles.name: Rotifera
version_4_profiles.etym: Latin rota, wheel, and ferre, bear
version_4_profiles.what: Microscopic wheel animals. Ciliated corona drives feeding currents.
version_4_profiles.traits: Ciliated corona drives feeding currents.

version_4_profiles.name: Nemertea
version_4_profiles.etym: Named for Nemertes, sea nymph of Greek myth
version_4_profiles.what: Ribbon worms with eversible proboscis. Unique fluid-driven proboscis system.
version_4_profiles.traits: Unique fluid-driven proboscis system.

version_4_profiles.name: Platyhelminthes
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek platys, flat, and helmins, worm
version_4_profiles.what: Flatworms and parasitic tapeworms. Flattened unsegmented bodies; no true body cavity.
version_4_profiles.traits: Flattened unsegmented bodies; no true body cavity.

version_4_profiles.name: Ecdysozoa
version_4_profiles.tagline: Molting animals from insects to nematodes
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek ekdysis, shedding, and zōon, animal
version_4_profiles.what: Molting animals from insects to nematodes. Shed external cuticle during growth.
version_4_profiles.traits: Shed external cuticle during growth.

version_4_profiles.name: Polychaeta
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek polys, many, and khaitē, bristle
version_4_profiles.what: Bristle-bearing marine annelid worms. Parapodia carrying numerous chaetae.
version_4_profiles.traits: Parapodia carrying numerous chaetae.

version_4_profiles.name: Malacostraca
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek malakos, soft, and ostrakon, shell
version_4_profiles.what: Crabs, lobsters, isopods and shrimp. Typically nineteen body segments.
version_4_profiles.traits: Typically nineteen body segments.

version_4_profiles.name: Cirripedia
version_4_profiles.etym: Latin cirrus, curl, and pes, foot
version_4_profiles.what: Barnacles and their relatives. Sessile suspension feeders with feathery legs.
version_4_profiles.traits: Sessile suspension feeders with feathery legs.

version_4_profiles.name: Copepoda
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek kōpē, oar, and pous, foot
version_4_profiles.what: Abundant planktonic crustaceans. Long antennae and rapid darting movement.
version_4_profiles.traits: Long antennae and rapid darting movement.

version_4_profiles.name: Isopoda
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek isos, equal, and pous, foot
version_4_profiles.what: Woodlice and marine isopods. Dorsoventrally flattened; legs of similar form.
version_4_profiles.traits: Dorsoventrally flattened; legs of similar form.

version_4_profiles.name: Amphipoda
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek amphi, on both sides, and pous, foot
version_4_profiles.what: Laterally compressed aquatic crustaceans. Differently specialized thoracic legs.
version_4_profiles.traits: Differently specialized thoracic legs.

version_4_profiles.name: Odonata
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek odōn, tooth
version_4_profiles.what: Dragonflies and damselflies. Large eyes; predatory aquatic nymphs.
version_4_profiles.traits: Large eyes; predatory aquatic nymphs.

version_4_profiles.name: Blattodea
version_4_profiles.etym: Latin blatta, cockroach
version_4_profiles.what: Cockroaches and termites. Flattened bodies or highly social colonies.
version_4_profiles.traits: Flattened bodies or highly social colonies.

version_4_profiles.name: Coleoptera
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek koleos, sheath, and pteron, wing
version_4_profiles.what: Beetles with hardened forewings. Elytra protect the membranous hindwings.
version_4_profiles.traits: Elytra protect the membranous hindwings.

version_4_profiles.name: Hymenoptera
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek hymēn, membrane, and pteron, wing
version_4_profiles.what: Ants, bees and wasps. Membranous paired wings; ovipositor variants.
version_4_profiles.traits: Membranous paired wings; ovipositor variants.

version_4_profiles.name: Lepidoptera
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek lepis, scale, and pteron, wing
version_4_profiles.what: Butterflies and moths. Scaly wings; proboscis in many adults.
version_4_profiles.traits: Scaly wings; proboscis in many adults.

version_4_profiles.name: Diptera
version_4_profiles.tagline: True flies with one wing pair
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek di, two, and pteron, wing
version_4_profiles.what: True flies with one wing pair. Hindwings modified into balancing halteres.
version_4_profiles.traits: Hindwings modified into balancing halteres.

version_4_profiles.name: Orthoptera
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek orthos, straight, and pteron, wing
version_4_profiles.what: Grasshoppers, crickets and katydids. Enlarged jumping hindlegs in many members.
version_4_profiles.traits: Enlarged jumping hindlegs in many members.

version_4_profiles.name: Asteroidea
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek astēr, star, and -oeidēs, resembling
version_4_profiles.what: Sea stars and relatives. Flexible arms and tube-feet locomotion.
version_4_profiles.traits: Flexible arms and tube-feet locomotion.

version_4_profiles.name: Ophiuroidea
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek ophis, serpent, and oura, tail
version_4_profiles.what: Brittle stars and basket stars. Distinct central disc; slender flexible arms.
version_4_profiles.traits: Distinct central disc; slender flexible arms.

version_4_profiles.name: Holothuroidea
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek holothourion, ancient sea-animal name
version_4_profiles.what: Soft-bodied sea cucumbers. Elongated body with reduced skeletal ossicles.
version_4_profiles.traits: Elongated body with reduced skeletal ossicles.

version_4_profiles.name: Octopoda
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek oktō, eight, and pous, foot
version_4_profiles.what: Eight-armed octopuses. Eight muscular arms; highly developed cognition.
version_4_profiles.traits: Eight muscular arms; highly developed cognition.

version_4_profiles.name: Teuthida
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek teuthis, squid
version_4_profiles.what: True squids. Eight arms plus two feeding tentacles.
version_4_profiles.traits: Eight arms plus two feeding tentacles.

version_4_profiles.name: Polyplacophora
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek polys, many, and plakos, plate
version_4_profiles.what: Chitons with eight dorsal plates. Eight shell valves and powerful gripping foot.
version_4_profiles.traits: Eight shell valves and powerful gripping foot.

version_4_profiles.name: Archaeocyatha
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek archaios, ancient, and kyathos, cup
version_4_profiles.what: Early Cambrian reef-building animals. Porous double-walled calcareous cups.
version_4_profiles.traits: Porous double-walled calcareous cups.

version_4_profiles.name: Myxini
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek myxa, slime
version_4_profiles.what: Hagfishes and jawless marine scavengers. Slime glands and keratinous tooth plates.
version_4_profiles.traits: Slime glands and keratinous tooth plates.

version_4_profiles.name: Petromyzontida
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek petra, stone, and myzō, suck
version_4_profiles.what: Lampreys with suction-cup mouths. Jawless oral discs; distinctive larval forms.
version_4_profiles.traits: Jawless oral discs; distinctive larval forms.

version_4_profiles.name: Heterostraci
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek heteros, different, and ostrakon, shell
version_4_profiles.what: Armored jawless Paleozoic fishes. Heavy head shields and varied mouth forms.
version_4_profiles.traits: Heavy head shields and varied mouth forms.

version_4_profiles.name: Thelodonti
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek thēlē, nipple, and odous, tooth
version_4_profiles.what: Small-scaled Paleozoic jawless fishes. Distinctive tiny dentine scales and varied body shapes.
version_4_profiles.traits: Distinctive tiny dentine scales and varied body shapes.

version_4_profiles.name: Acanthodii
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek akantha, spine
version_4_profiles.what: Spiny-finned early jawed fishes. Bony spines before several fins.
version_4_profiles.traits: Bony spines before several fins.

version_4_profiles.name: Osteichthyes
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek osteon, bone, and ichthys, fish
version_4_profiles.what: Bony fishes and tetrapod descendants. Endochondral bone and ancestral lungs or swim bladder.
version_4_profiles.traits: Endochondral bone and ancestral lungs or swim bladder.

version_4_profiles.name: Elasmobranchii
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek elasma, metal plate, and branchia, gills
version_4_profiles.what: Sharks, skates and rays. Cartilaginous skeleton; continuously renewed teeth.
version_4_profiles.traits: Cartilaginous skeleton; continuously renewed teeth.

version_4_profiles.name: Holocephali
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek holos, whole, and kephalē, head
version_4_profiles.what: Chimaeras and fossil relatives. Upper jaw fused to skull in living forms.
version_4_profiles.traits: Upper jaw fused to skull in living forms.

version_4_profiles.name: Teleostei
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek teleios, complete, and osteon, bone
version_4_profiles.what: Most modern ray-finned fish species. Mobile jaws and lightweight skeletons.
version_4_profiles.traits: Mobile jaws and lightweight skeletons.

version_4_profiles.name: Acipenseriformes
version_4_profiles.etym: Latin acipenser, sturgeon, and -formes, shape
version_4_profiles.what: Sturgeons and paddlefish. Mostly cartilaginous internal skeletons; heterocercal tails.
version_4_profiles.traits: Mostly cartilaginous internal skeletons; heterocercal tails.

version_4_profiles.name: Tetrapodomorpha
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek tetra, four, and pous, foot, plus morphē
version_4_profiles.what: Lobe-finned ancestry of land vertebrates. Limb-bone precursors in paired fins.
version_4_profiles.traits: Limb-bone precursors in paired fins.

version_4_profiles.name: Reptiliomorpha
version_4_profiles.etym: Latin reptilis, creeping, and Greek morphē, form
version_4_profiles.what: Tetrapod line leading toward amniotes. Progressively terrestrial vertebral and limb traits.
version_4_profiles.traits: Progressively terrestrial vertebral and limb traits.

version_4_profiles.name: Parareptilia
version_4_profiles.tagline: Ancient reptile branch with diverse herbivores
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek para, beside, and reptilis, reptile
version_4_profiles.what: Ancient reptile branch with diverse herbivores. Broad skulls and multiple forms of dermal armor.
version_4_profiles.traits: Broad skulls and multiple forms of dermal armor.

version_4_profiles.name: Sauropsida
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek saura, lizard, and opsis, aspect
version_4_profiles.what: Reptile line including birds. Amniote branch encompassing living reptiles and birds.
version_4_profiles.traits: Amniote branch encompassing living reptiles and birds.

version_4_profiles.name: Diapsida
version_4_profiles.tagline: Major reptile lineage with two temporal openings
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek di, two, and apsis, arch
version_4_profiles.what: Major reptile lineage with two temporal openings. Ancestral paired skull fenestrae; many later modifications.
version_4_profiles.traits: Ancestral paired skull fenestrae; many later modifications.

version_4_profiles.name: Archosauromorpha
version_4_profiles.tagline: Reptile line toward crocodiles and birds
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek archōn, ruler, saura, lizard, morphē, form
version_4_profiles.what: Reptile line toward crocodiles and birds. Archosaur-style ankle and skull traits in derived members.
version_4_profiles.traits: Archosaur-style ankle and skull traits in derived members.

version_4_profiles.name: Phytosauria
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek phyton, plant, and saura, lizard; historic misinterpretation
version_4_profiles.what: Long-snouted crocodile-like Triassic reptiles. Nostrils positioned high near eyes.
version_4_profiles.traits: Nostrils positioned high near eyes.

version_4_profiles.name: Rauisuchia
version_4_profiles.etym: Named for fossil collector Wilhelm Rau
version_4_profiles.what: Large predatory Triassic pseudosuchians. Deep skulls; often erect limbs.
version_4_profiles.traits: Deep skulls; often erect limbs.

version_4_profiles.name: Ornithodira
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek ornis, bird, and deirē, neck
version_4_profiles.what: Dinosaur and pterosaur lineage. Elongated limb posture and specialized ankles.
version_4_profiles.traits: Elongated limb posture and specialized ankles.

version_4_profiles.name: Diplodocidae
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek diplos, double, and dokos, beam
version_4_profiles.what: Long-necked Jurassic sauropods. Very long tails and peg-like teeth.
version_4_profiles.traits: Very long tails and peg-like teeth.

version_4_profiles.name: Titanosauria
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek Titan, mythic giant, and saura, lizard
version_4_profiles.what: Giant Late Cretaceous sauropods. Wide-gauge stance; diverse armored and unarmored forms.
version_4_profiles.traits: Wide-gauge stance; diverse armored and unarmored forms.

version_4_profiles.name: Ankylosauria
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek ankylos, fused, and saura, lizard
version_4_profiles.what: Armored herbivorous dinosaurs. Rows of bony osteoderms; some tail clubs.
version_4_profiles.traits: Rows of bony osteoderms; some tail clubs.

version_4_profiles.name: Stegosauria
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek stegos, roof, and saura, lizard
version_4_profiles.what: Plated herbivorous dinosaurs. Back plates and spiked tail defenses.
version_4_profiles.traits: Back plates and spiked tail defenses.

version_4_profiles.name: Pachycephalosauria
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek pachys, thick, and kephalē, head
version_4_profiles.what: Dome-headed Cretaceous dinosaurs. Thickened skull roof and bipedal posture.
version_4_profiles.traits: Thickened skull roof and bipedal posture.

version_4_profiles.name: Tyrannosauroidea
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek tyrannos, ruler, and saura, lizard
version_4_profiles.what: Predatory dinosaurs culminating in tyrannosaurs. Deep skulls and two-fingered forelimbs in derived taxa.
version_4_profiles.traits: Deep skulls and two-fingered forelimbs in derived taxa.

version_4_profiles.name: Dromaeosauridae
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek dromaios, running, and saura, lizard
version_4_profiles.what: Feathered sickle-clawed theropods. Enlarged second-toe claw; bird-like wrist.
version_4_profiles.traits: Enlarged second-toe claw; bird-like wrist.

version_4_profiles.name: Avialae
version_4_profiles.etym: Latin avis, bird, and Greek ala, wing

version_4_profiles.traits: Flight-feather evolution and specialized forelimbs.

version_4_profiles.name: Neornithes
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek neos, new, and ornithes, birds
version_4_profiles.what: Crown-group modern birds. Living bird last common ancestor and descendants.
version_4_profiles.traits: Living bird last common ancestor and descendants.

version_4_profiles.name: Passeriformes
version_4_profiles.etym: Latin passer, sparrow, and -formes, shaped
version_4_profiles.what: Perching songbirds and relatives. Anisodactyl feet and highly developed vocal systems.
version_4_profiles.traits: Anisodactyl feet and highly developed vocal systems.

version_4_profiles.name: Theria
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek thērion, wild beast
version_4_profiles.what: Marsupials and placental mammals. Live birth in most lineages; specialized ear regions.
version_4_profiles.traits: Live birth in most lineages; specialized ear regions.

version_4_profiles.name: Metatheria
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek meta, beyond, and thērion, beast
version_4_profiles.what: Marsupials and extinct relatives. Distinctive reproductive and dental patterns.
version_4_profiles.traits: Distinctive reproductive and dental patterns.

version_4_profiles.name: Eutheria
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek eu, true, and thērion, beast
version_4_profiles.what: Placental mammals and fossil relatives. Extended gestation in crown placentals.
version_4_profiles.traits: Extended gestation in crown placentals.

version_4_profiles.name: Xenarthra
version_4_profiles.etym: Greek xenos, strange, and arthron, joint
version_4_profiles.what: Sloths, anteaters and armadillos. Additional vertebral articulations in many members.
version_4_profiles.traits: Additional vertebral articulations in many members.

version_4_profiles.name: Afrotheria
version_4_profiles.etym: Africa + Greek thērion, beast
version_4_profiles.what: Elephants, hyraxes, tenrecs and allies. African-rooted molecularly supported placental radiation.
version_4_profiles.traits: African-rooted molecularly supported placental radiation.

version_4_profiles.name: Carnivora
version_4_profiles.etym: Latin caro, flesh, and vorare, devour
version_4_profiles.what: Cats, dogs, bears and seals. Carnassial teeth in many lineages.
version_4_profiles.traits: Carnassial teeth in many lineages.

version_4_profiles.name: Rodentia
version_4_profiles.tagline: Gnawing mammals from mice to capybaras
version_4_profiles.etym: Latin rodere, gnaw
version_4_profiles.what: Gnawing mammals from mice to capybaras. Ever-growing incisors and diastema.
version_4_profiles.traits: Ever-growing incisors and diastema.
